AirScroll needs this service to scroll on your behalf inside other apps. It does not read the content of your screen: it only sees which app is in the foreground, and sends the swipe gestures that your hand movement produces.
Turns hand movement into scrolling, offline.
Open source · Everything runs offline on your phone
Since Android 13, apps installed outside an app store cannot turn on the accessibility service until you unlock it once. If the switch looks greyed out, or you see \"Restricted setting\", do this:
Open the app info with the button below.
Tap the three dots in the top right corner.
Tap \"Allow restricted settings\", then come back here.

Play Protect may also call AirScroll harmful. It flags any sideloaded app that asks for the camera together with the accessibility service — the combination stalkerware uses. AirScroll has no internet permission at all and the code is public, so you can check for yourself. Choose \"Install anyway\" to continue.
It is what sees your hand. The images stay inside this app for the time of one frame: nothing is saved, nothing is sent.
It is the only way an app can scroll inside another app. AirScroll asks for the smallest version of it: it can send gestures, it cannot read your screen.
Three details that make it work well
None of them is mandatory, but without them something will feel broken.
Instead of asking you to guess numbers, AirScroll measures your real hand: how far you hold it, how much it shakes, how wide your comfortable movement is.
Fake content that really scrolls with your hand, right inside the app. No accessibility service needed, so you can check that the gestures work before anything else.
Try the gestures without leaving the app
Same engine as the real thing, on fake content. The best place to tune sensitivity and dead zone.
Move these while you scroll: the effect is immediate, and what you set here is what the real thing will do.
Scroll your hand up and down. The text follows you, exactly as if a finger were resting on the screen and dragging it.
There are no jumps and no commands. What the camera sees is a position, and that position becomes a speed: the further your hand goes from the resting point, the faster the page moves.
Around the resting point there is a dead zone, shaped on the tremor measured during calibration. Inside it nothing happens, which is why holding still keeps the page still.
Only one axis moves at a time. Once the vertical takes over, sideways drift is ignored until you come back to the middle — otherwise scrolling would keep changing the volume by accident.
If your hand slowly drifts while you read, the resting point drifts with it. It is a small thing that avoids the most annoying failure: a page that scrolls on its own because your arm got tired.
Close your fist for about two seconds to stop. Out there, in a real app, leaving the app stops it too, and the camera closes with it.
And here is something to scroll past
Busy hands? Wider dead zone and calmer scrolling, for recipes.
Yellow · waiting for a thumbs up
Hand at 20-30 cm. Wide movements, gentler response.
Hand at 40-60 cm. The balanced choice.
Hand beyond 70 cm. Small movements, stronger response.
Follows the hand size seen by the camera, using your calibration.
Frames are being sent but the model is not answering. This is a bug, not your hand: please report it with this screen.
Records how your hand looks to the model, so the thresholds can be tuned on real numbers instead of guesses.
Five short takes. Only numbers are saved — the 21 hand points and the recognised gesture. No image is ever written to the file, and nothing leaves your phone unless you choose to share it.
The file is on your phone. Open it if you want to see exactly what it contains: it is plain text.
Hold a thumbs up steady, the way you would to start scrolling.
Close your fist and hold it, the way you would to stop.
Open hand, still. This teaches the app what should NOT start anything.
Move your hand up and down as if scrolling, at your natural pace.
Lower your hand or move it out of frame. This shows what the camera sees when you are not asking for anything.
AirScroll speaks Italian, English, Spanish, German and Chinese. \"System\" follows your phone.
Hand recognition could not start: the recognition model is not inside this build. The camera works, but no gesture will ever be detected.

Hand recognition could not start: the recognition library could not be loaded on this phone.
Hand recognition could not start. The technical details are below: please send them, they say exactly what went wrong.

Hold your hand still in front of the camera, at the distance you would normally use. Two and a half seconds: this measures how much your hand trembles and how big it looks, and marks your resting point.
Move your hand outwards in every direction, as if drawing a circle in the air. Each segment lights up when you reach it. Move as far as is comfortable — not as far as you possibly can.
This is far enough for me
Reach measured: %1$d up, %2$d down, %3$d left, %4$d right. They are different, and that is the point: scrolling now asks each direction only what your hand can actually do.
Open hand, palm towards the screen, 20 to 40 cm away — the distance you will actually use.
Move your whole forearm, not just your fingers: recognition follows the middle of your palm.
One slow lap, about five seconds. Moving fast makes the camera lose your hand.
Go as far as is comfortable, not as far as you can strain. This should look like the way you will really use it.
Stay inside the frame. If the dot turns red, the camera has lost you: come back towards the middle.
Every gesture, moving. The details are the ones that are not obvious the first time.

Hold it for about half a second, not just a flash. A brief dip — your hand rotates, a finger covers the thumb — does not reset the count: it picks up again. But clearly making a different gesture does reset it, because that means you changed your mind.

Speed is progressive: a small movement scrolls slowly, a wide one scrolls fast. Small tremors do nothing at all — the neutral zone measured during calibration absorbs them. And each direction only asks for what your hand can actually reach.

One axis at a time: while you are scrolling you cannot change the volume by accident, and the other axis has to win by a clear margin to take over. The horizontal axis can also be switched off entirely in Settings.
Two seconds, so you do not stop by accident. Adjustable in Settings → Timings. Opening your hand before the two seconds are up cancels the stop.

The amber window also closes on its own after about six seconds without a thumbs up, and the camera goes off. To reopen it without leaving the app, tap “Look for the hand” on the AirScroll notification.
The page goes where you put your hand and stays there, as if you were dragging it. Push further and it keeps scrolling; flick your hand back and it carries on and slows down.
Your hand sets the speed: the further from centre, the faster it scrolls, and it keeps going until you come back. This is how it worked up to version 0.4.5.
The manual and the privacy notice travel inside the app: AirScroll cannot reach the network, and a document explaining exactly that would be a contradiction if you needed a connection to read it.
The document could not be opened. There may be no PDF reader installed.
